chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from al-Husayn ibn Mayyah, from Umayya ibn Amr, from al-Sha'iri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to say: 'When the caller calls out, it is not for you to increase (your call), and rather the call makes the increase prohibited, and silence makes it permissible.'

key_terms.الْمُنَادِي: The caller (one who announces goods for sale)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on increasing bids or calls in the market after a seller has already called out?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the classical Islamic commercial rule of 'nidā' (public call), where the first bidder's offer becomes exclusive to prevent chaotic competition. It reflects the practical jurisprudence of early Islamic markets, emphasizing that silence by the initial bidder allows others to compete, thereby ensuring transparency and fairness in trade transactions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of our companions, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Al Husayn Bin Mayyah, from Umayya Bin Amro, from Al Ashary,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘When the caller calls out (in the market to sell his goods), so it is not for you that you increase (upon his call), and rather the increased calling makes it Prohibited, and silence makes it Permissible’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from certain persons of our people from Mansur ibn al-‘ Abbas from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from al-Husayn ibn Mayyah from ‘Umayyah ibn ‘Amr form al-Sha‘iyriy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, ‘If one is calling to what he sells, you do not have to increase; only announcing makes increasing unlawful and remaining silent makes the increase lawful.’”
